slug: afl
title: "AFL: Coverage-guided Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement the core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) fuzzing algorithm with full paper-faithful

=============== requirements/aflfast.yaml
slug: aflfast
title: "AFLFast: Power Schedules via Markov Chain Model"
description: |
  Implement AFLFast's power schedules based on modeling fuzzing as a Markov chain.
  Each unique execution path is a state; mutations cause transitions between states.
  The key insight is that AFL's constant energy wastes effort on high-frequency paths.
  AFLFast assigns energy inversely proportional to path frequency f(i) and exponentially
  in selection count s(i). Includes: EXPLOIT schedule (p(i)=alpha, same as AFL),
  EXPLORE schedule (p(i)=alpha/beta, normalized), COE schedule (cut-off exponential:
  skip seeds with f(i)>mu, otherwise min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i), M)), FAST schedule
  (recommended: min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)), LINEAR schedule (min(alpha/beta *
  s(i)/f(i), M)), QUAD schedule (min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2/f(i), M)). Also implements
  PathFrequencyTracker (Markov state identification, transition counting, rare path
  detection), seed prioritization strategies (prioritize_small_s for FAST/COE,
  prioritize_small_f for explore/linear/quad), EnergyComputer with Gini coefficient
  analysis, and schedule comparison utilities.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py
  - fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - Markov chain path model
  - path frequency tracking (f(i) = inputs exercising path i)
  - selection count tracking (s(i) = times seed i was chosen)
  - power schedule variants (FAST, COE, explore, exploit, linear, quad)
  - energy assignment formulas (exponential, linear, quadratic)
  - cut-off mechanism (skip over-fuzzed seeds)
  - upper bound M on energy (prevent explosion)
  - seed prioritization by s(i) and f(i)
  - Markov state transitions and probability estimation
  - rare path identification and bonus
  - energy distribution analysis (Gini coefficient)
expected_outputs:
  AFLFAST_PATHS_FAST: 10
  AFLFAST_PATHS_COE: 10
  AFLFAST_SPEEDUP: 1.00
  AFLFAST_MEAN_ENERGY: 198.5
=============== requirements/aflgo.yaml
slug: aflgo
title: "AFLGo: Directed Greybox Fuzzing"
description: |
  Implement AFLGo's directed greybox fuzzing with distance-based seed prioritization
  and simulated annealing for exploration-to-exploitation transition. Two-level distance
  computation: (1) Function-level via BFS on reverse call graph from target functions,
  (2) Basic-block level combining CFG shortest paths with function distances via harmonic
  mean. CallGraph class with function/edge management. CFGDistance class with BFS-based
  shortest path computation. Distance normalization to [0,1] range. Seed distance via
  minimum block distance among covered edges. Simulated annealing with exponential cooling
  schedule T(t)=T0*alpha^(t/t_x*K), plus alternative cooling schedules (linear: T0*(1-t/t_x),
  logarithmic: T0/(1+log(1+t/t_x*K)), adaptive: adjusts alpha based on progress). Energy
  assignment formula: p(s,T)=base*((1-d(s))*(1-T)+0.5*T) transitioning from uniform (T=1)
  to distance-proportional (T=0). Seed skipping during exploitation phase (T<0.3, d>0.9).
  DistanceComputer class orchestrating the full pipeline. Phase detection (exploration/
  transition/exploitation).
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_distance.py
  - fuzzsim/aflgo_annealing.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/aflgo_experiment.py

  - run.sh

  - directed greybox fuzzing
  - call graph construction and BFS traversal
  - CFG shortest path computation
  - function-level distance via reverse BFS
  - basic-block level distance via harmonic mean
  - distance normalization to [0,1]
  - seed distance aggregation (minimum, harmonic mean)
  - simulated annealing (exponential cooling)
  - alternative cooling schedules (linear, logarithmic, adaptive)
  - exploration vs exploitation phases
  - temperature-based energy assignment
  - seed skipping during exploitation
  - time-to-exposure (TTE) metric

slug: aflpp
title: "AFL++: Modular Fuzzing Framework"
description: |
  Implement AFL++'s modular framework with full custom mutator API and MOpt PSO-based
  mutation scheduling. Custom Mutator API matching AFL++ afl-fuzz-mutator.c: init(),
  fuzz(buf, add_buf), fuzz_count(buf), havoc_mutation(buf, max_size),
  havoc_mutation_probability(), post_process(buf), trim(buf), describe(),
  queue_new_entry(buf, coverage). MutatorRegistry: register/unregister mutators,
  weighted random selection, dynamic weight adjustment (1.1x on success, 0.99x on
  failure, min 0.1). Built-in mutators: GrammarMutator (token templates, structured
  input generation, grammar-aware trimming), CmpLogMutator (RedQueen comparison
  operand recording and substitution for bypassing magic bytes). MOpt PSO scheduler:
  pilot phase (independent operator testing, L iterations each), core phase (PSO
  velocity update: v=w*v+c1*r1*(pbest-x)+c2*r2*(gbest-x), position update: x=x+v,
  velocity clamping [-0.3, 0.3], probability bounds [0.02, 0.50], normalization to
  valid distribution). Operator set: bit_flip, byte_flip, arith_add, arith_sub,
  interesting, random_byte, havoc_1, havoc_2. Personal/global best tracking, fitness
  history, convergence monitoring. PowerScheduleEnsemble: rotate through FAST/COE/

slug: fairfuzz
title: "FairFuzz: Targeted Mutation for Rare Branches"
description: |
  Implement FairFuzz's approach to improving coverage of rare branches by identifying
  under-covered edges, detecting input-to-branch influence via differential mutation,
  and applying targeted mutations that preserve rare branch hits. Rare branch
  identification: count seeds per edge, edges with count <= threshold are "rare".
  Both fixed threshold (absolute cutoff) and dynamic threshold (percentile of hit count
  distribution) supported. RareBranchTracker with incremental updates and statistics.
  Influence detection (mutation masking): for each byte position, probe with random
  replacements and measure whether target branch coverage is destroyed. If >60% of
  probes destroy coverage, the byte is "influential" and must be preserved. Fast
  variant with early termination. InfluenceDetector class with caching (hash-based
  cache key: data_hash + target_branch). Masked mutation: apply havoc-like operations
  only to safe (non-influential) positions while preserving critical bytes. Branch
  selection strategy: prefer rare branches already hit by the seed (preservation is
  meaningful), among candidates pick the rarest. Rarity scores normalized to [0,1]
  for weighted targeting.
depends_on:
  - afl
files_to_create:
  - fuzzsim/fairfuzz_rare.py
  - fuzzsim/fairfuzz_mask.py
  - fuzzsim/experiments/fairfuzz_experiment.py
files_to_modify:
  - run.sh
concepts:
  - rare branch identification (edges hit by few seeds)

"""Core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) coverage-guided greybox fuzzer.

This module is a faithful, deterministic simulation of afl-fuzz.c's algorithm:

* 64KB shared-memory edge bitmap with hit-count bucketing
  (1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+),
* edge identification via ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` (AFL's
  ``prev_loc``/``cur_loc`` trick, usually written ``(prev ^ cur) >> 1``),
* a fork-server model that amortises target start-up cost,
* test-case calibration with multi-run stability detection,
* input trimming with powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage,
* corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest + fastest entry per edge),
* the complete deterministic stage pipeline (walking bit flips 1/2/4, byte
  flips 8/16/32, arithmetics +/- 1..35 for 8/16/32 bit widths in both
  endiannesses, interesting values 8/16/32, auto-dictionary extraction during
  the bit-flip stage and user/auto dictionary insertion),
* the havoc stage (2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations),
* the splice stage (midpoint recombination of two queue entries + havoc),
* performance scoring from execution speed / bitmap size / depth / handicap,
* crash de-duplication through coverage hashing,
* and queue scheduling with favoured-seed priority (the 75/25 skip split).

Everything is driven from a single ``numpy.random.RandomState`` so that a given
seed always produces the same run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import numpy as np

from fuzzsim.bitmap import MAP_SIZE
from fuzzsim.mutation import (
    INTERESTING_8,
    INTERESTING_16,
    INTERESTING_32,
    clone_bytes,
    delete_bytes,
    insert_bytes,
)
from fuzzsim.seed import TestCase

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AFL tuning constants (config.h)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ARITH_MAX = 35            # maximum offset used by the arithmetic stages
HAVOC_STACK_POW2 = 7      # havoc stacks 2^1 .. 2^7 mutations
HAVOC_CYCLES = 256        # base havoc iterations (scaled by performance score)
HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT = 1024  # havoc iterations when deterministic stages are off
HAVOC_MIN = 16            # never do fewer than this many havoc execs
HAVOC_MAX_MULT = 16       # performance score cap multiplier (=> max 1600)
HAVOC_BLK_SMALL = 32
HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM = 128
HAVOC_BLK_LARGE = 1500
SPLICE_CYCLES = 15        # splice attempts per queue entry
SPLICE_HAVOC = 32         # havoc iterations applied to a spliced input

SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB = 75     # favoured/unseen entries: 75/25 split
SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB = 95   # skip probability for old non-favoured entries
SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB = 75   # skip probability for fresh non-favoured entries

CAL_CYCLES = 3            # calibration executions for a fresh entry
TRIM_MIN_BYTES = 4
TRIM_START_STEPS = 16
TRIM_END_STEPS = 1024

MIN_AUTO_EXTRA = 3
MAX_AUTO_EXTRA = 32
MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS = 50      # auto dictionary capacity
MAX_DET_EXTRAS = 200      # deterministic extras cut-off

# Hit-count buckets used by AFL's classify_counts().
COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS: Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int], ...] = (
    (0, 0, 0),        # never executed
    (1, 1, 1),        # exactly once
    (2, 2, 2),        # twice
    (3, 3, 4),        # three times
    (4, 7, 8),        # 4-7
    (8, 15, 16),      # 8-15
    (16, 31, 32),     # 16-31
    (32, 127, 64),    # 32-127
    (128, 1 << 30, 128),  # 128+
)


def classify_counts(count: int) -> int:
    """Map a raw hit count onto AFL's 8 hit-count buckets.

    AFL folds hit counts into powers-of-two-ish buckets so that small changes
    in loop trip counts do not look like new coverage::

        1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+
    """
    if count < 0:
        raise ValueError("hit count must be non-negative")
    for low, high, bucket in COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS:
        if low <= count <= high:
            return bucket
    return 128


def bucket_index(count: int) -> int:
    """Return the index (0..8) of the bucket a hit count falls into."""
    for idx, (low, high, _bucket) in enumerate(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS):
        if low <= count <= high:
            return idx
    return len(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS) - 1


def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE) -> int:
    """Compute AFL's edge id for the transition ``prev_block -> cur_block``.

    AFL's instrumentation keeps ``prev_loc`` already shifted right by one so
    that A->B and B->A hash differently; the transition is therefore
    ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` taken modulo the bitmap size.
    """
    return ((prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block) % map_size


def coverage_hash(edges: Iterable[int]) -> str:
    """Stable hash of a coverage set, used for crash de-duplication."""
    payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
    return hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:16]


def swap16(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 16 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFF
    return ((value & 0xFF) << 8) | (value >> 8)


def swap32(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 32 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return (
        ((value & 0x000000FF) << 24)
        | ((value & 0x0000FF00) << 8)
        | ((value & 0x00FF0000) >> 8)
        | ((value & 0xFF000000) >> 24)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Could this value have been produced by a cheaper stage?" predicates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``xor_val`` is reachable by the walking bit-flip stages."""
    if xor_val == 0:
        return True
    # Shift right until we hit the first set bit.
    sh = 0
    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
        sh += 1
        xor_val >>= 1
    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15, 255):
        return True
    # 16 and 32 bit flips are only tried on aligned offsets.
    if xor_val == 0xFFFF and sh % 16 == 0:
        return True
    if xor_val == 0xFFFFFFFF and sh % 32 == 0:
        return True
    return False


def could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the arithmetic stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    diffs = 0
    ov = nv = 0
    for i in range(blen):
        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b

    # A single byte differs: an 8 bit arithmetic op would have found it.
    if diffs == 1:
        if abs(ov - nv) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True

    if blen == 1:
        return False

    # Try 16 bit arithmetics in both endiannesses.
    diffs = 0
    for i in range(blen // 2):
        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b
    if diffs == 1:
        if abs(ov - nv) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
        if abs(swap16(ov) - swap16(nv)) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True

    if blen == 4:
        if abs(old_val - new_val) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
        if abs(swap32(old_val) - swap32(new_val)) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
    return False


def could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the interesting-value stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    # Single-byte interesting values applied at any offset.
    for i in range(blen):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_8:
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((interesting & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True

    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
        return False

    for i in range(blen - 1):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_16:
            iv = interesting & 0xFFFF
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (iv << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True
            if blen > 2:
                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swap16(iv) << (8 * i))
                if new_val == tval:
                    return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fork server simulation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ForkServer:
    """Simulated AFL fork server.

    The real fork server executes the target up to ``main()`` once and then
    clones the initialised process for every test case, which removes the
    (expensive) linking/initialisation cost from the per-exec budget.  We model
    that: ``STARTUP_COST`` is paid once at ``start()`` and every subsequent run
    only pays ``FORK_COST`` plus the target's own execution time.
    """

    STARTUP_COST = 0.020  # 20ms one-off initialisation
    FORK_COST = 0.0002    # 0.2ms per fork
    EXECVE_COST = 0.010   # 10ms if we had to execve() every time

    def __init__(self, program):
        self.program = program
        self.is_running = False
        self.total_execs = 0
        self.total_time = 0.0
        self.startup_time = 0.0
        self.timeouts = 0
        self.child_pid = 0

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Spin up the fork server (paid once)."""
        if self.is_running:
            return
        self.is_running = True
        self.startup_time = self.STARTUP_COST
        self.total_time += self.STARTUP_COST
        self.child_pid = 1000

    def run(self, data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Execute one test case through the fork server."""
        if not self.is_running:
            self.start()
        self.child_pid += 1
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.program.execute(data)
        self.total_execs += 1
        self.total_time += self.FORK_COST + exec_time
        return set(edges), bool(is_crash), float(exec_time)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.is_running = False
        self.child_pid = 0

    @property
    def saved_time(self) -> float:
        """Time saved compared to a plain execve() based executor."""
        return self.total_execs * (self.EXECVE_COST - self.FORK_COST) - self.STARTUP_COST


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bitmap with hit-count bucketing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AFLBitmap:
    """64KB coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing and virgin-bit tracking."""

    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
        self.map_size = map_size
        # virgin_bits[edge] is the OR of every bucket value observed so far.
        self.virgin_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
        self.hit_counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.trace_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}

    # -- current run ------------------------------------------------------
    def reset_trace(self) -> None:
        self.trace_bits = {}

    def record_trace(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> None:
        """Store the raw hit counts of the current execution."""
        self.trace_bits = dict(edges)

    def classified_trace(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
        """Return the current trace after classify_counts()."""
        return {e: classify_counts(c) for e, c in self.trace_bits.items()}

    # -- global bitmap ----------------------------------------------------
    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
        """AFL's has_new_bits(): 2 = new edge, 1 = new hit-count bucket, 0 = nothing."""
        result = 0
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            bucket = classify_counts(count)
            seen = self.virgin_bits.get(edge, 0)
            if seen == 0:
                return 2
            if seen & bucket == 0:
                result = max(result, 1)
        return result

    def update(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
        """Fold an execution into the global bitmap, returning new edges."""
        new_edges = set()
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            if edge not in self.virgin_bits:
                new_edges.add(edge)
                self.virgin_bits[edge] = 0
            self.virgin_bits[edge] |= classify_counts(count)
            self.global_coverage.add(edge)
            self.hit_counts[edge] = self.hit_counts.get(edge, 0) + count
        return new_edges

    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
        """Number of non-zero bytes in the bitmap (AFL's count_bytes)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
        if total_edges == 0:
            return 0.0
        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0

    def map_density(self) -> float:
        """Fraction of the 64KB map that is in use (AFL's map density stat)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage) / self.map_size * 100.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Dictionary:
    """User (``-x``) and auto-extracted dictionary tokens."""

    def __init__(self, extras: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None):
        self.extras: List[bytes] = sorted(set(extras or []), key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        self.auto_extras: List[bytes] = []
        self.auto_hits: Dict[bytes, int] = {}

    def maybe_add_auto(self, token: bytes) -> bool:
        """AFL's maybe_add_auto(): remember a token found during bit flipping."""
        if not (MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= len(token) <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA):
            return False
        if len(set(token)) <= 1:  # all-same bytes carry no information
            return False
        if token in self.extras:
            return False
        if token in self.auto_hits:
            self.auto_hits[token] += 1
            return False
        self.auto_hits[token] = 1
        if len(self.auto_extras) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS:
            self.auto_extras.append(token)
            self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
            return True
        # Replace the least useful (largest) entry.
        self.auto_extras[-1] = token
        self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        return True

    @property
    def all_tokens(self) -> List[bytes]:

        self.cur_depth = 0
        self.max_depth = 0
        self.coverage_history: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []  # (execs, edges)
        self.queue_history: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []     # (execs, corpus size)
        self.current_stage = "init"
        self.current_target: Optional[TestCase] = None
        self.stability_samples: List[float] = []

        self.fork_server.start()
        for data in seeds or [b"hello world"]:
            self.add_seed(bytes(data))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Setup helpers
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _infer_total_edges(self) -> int:
        for attr in ("get_total_edges", "total_edges"):
            value = getattr(self.program, attr, None)
            if callable(value):
                return int(value())
            if isinstance(value, int):
                return value
        return MAP_SIZE

    def add_seed(self, data: bytes) -> TestCase:
        """Add an initial seed: execute, calibrate, trim and queue it."""
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.run_target(data)
        tc = TestCase(
            data=data,
            coverage=set(edges),
            exec_time=exec_time,
            is_crash=is_crash,
            depth=0,
            creation_time=self.total_execs,
        )
        self.bitmap.update({e: 1 for e in edges})
        self.queue.append(tc)
        self.queued_discovered += 1
        self.calibrate_case(tc)
        if self.use_trim:
            self.trim_case(tc)
        self.update_bitmap_score(tc)
        self._record_history()
        return tc

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Execution
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def budget_left(self) -> int:
        return max(0, self.max_execs - self.total_execs)

    def out_of_budget(self) -> bool:
        return self.total_execs >= self.max_execs

    def run_target(self, data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Run the target once through the fork server and account for it."""
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.fork_server.run(data)
        self.total_execs += 1
        self.stage_execs[self.current_stage] = self.stage_execs.get(self.current_stage, 0) + 1
        self.bitmap.record_trace({e: 1 for e in edges})
        if is_crash:
            self.total_crashes += 1
            if self.first_crash_exec is None:
                self.first_crash_exec = self.total_execs
        return edges, is_crash, exec_time

    def common_fuzz_stuff(self, data: bytes, parent: Optional[TestCase] = None) -> bool:
        """Execute a mutated buffer and queue it when it is interesting."""
        if self.out_of_budget():
            return False
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.run_target(data)
        return self.save_if_interesting(data, edges, is_crash, exec_time, parent)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Queue management
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def save_if_interesting(
        self,
        data: bytes,
        edges: Set[int],
        is_crash: bool,
        exec_time: float,
        parent: Optional[TestCase] = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """AFL's save_if_interesting(): queue new coverage, de-duplicate crashes."""
        trace = {e: 1 for e in edges}
        is_new = False

        if is_crash:
            chash = coverage_hash(edges)
            if chash not in self.unique_crash_hashes:
                crash_tc = TestCase(
                    data=data,
                    coverage=set(edges),
                    exec_time=exec_time,
                    is_crash=True,
                    depth=(parent.depth + 1) if parent else 0,
                    creation_time=self.total_execs,
                )
                self.unique_crash_hashes[chash] = crash_tc
                self.crashes.append(crash_tc)

        new_level = self.bitmap.has_new_bits(trace)
        if new_level > 0:
            self.bitmap.update(trace)
            tc = TestCase(
                data=data,
                coverage=set(edges),
                exec_time=exec_time,
                is_crash=is_crash,
                depth=(parent.depth + 1) if parent else 0,
                creation_time=self.total_execs,
            )
            self.queue.append(tc)
            self.queued_discovered += 1
            self.max_depth = max(self.max_depth, tc.depth)
            self.calibrate_case(tc)
            if self.use_trim:
                self.trim_case(tc)
            self.update_bitmap_score(tc)
            self.stage_finds[self.current_stage] = self.stage_finds.get(self.current_stage, 0) + 1
            is_new = True
        self._record_history()
        return is_new

    def _record_history(self) -> None:
        self.coverage_history.append((self.total_execs, self.bitmap.get_coverage_count()))
        self.queue_history.append((self.total_execs, len(self.queue)))

    def calibrate_case(self, tc: TestCase, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> float:
        """Run a fresh entry several times: stability detection + timing.

        Stability is the Jaccard similarity of the coverage observed across
        runs; anything below 100% means the target has non-deterministic edges
        (AFL calls those "variable" and marks the entry).
        """
        traces: List[Set[int]] = []
        total_time = 0.0
        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                break
            edges, _crash, exec_time = self.run_target(tc.data)
            traces.append(set(edges))
            total_time += exec_time
        if not traces:
            return 100.0

        union: Set[int] = set()
        intersection: Optional[Set[int]] = None
        for t in traces:
            union |= t
            intersection = set(t) if intersection is None else (intersection & t)
        intersection = intersection or set()
        stability = 100.0 if not union else len(intersection) / len(union) * 100.0

        tc.exec_time = total_time / len(traces)
        tc.coverage = set(union)
        tc.is_variable = stability < 100.0  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        tc.stability = stability            # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        self.stability_samples.append(stability)
        return stability

    def trim_case(self, tc: TestCase) -> int:
        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the entry's coverage."""
        if len(tc.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
            return 0

        original_len = len(tc.data)
        reference = set(tc.coverage)
        data = bytearray(tc.data)

        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, (len(data) - 1).bit_length())
        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)

        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, 1) and remove_len > 0:
            pos = 0
            while pos + remove_len <= len(data):
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    break
                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + remove_len:])
                if not candidate:
                    pos += remove_len
                    continue
                edges, _crash, exec_time = self.run_target(candidate)
                if set(edges) == reference:
                    data = bytearray(candidate)
                    tc.exec_time = exec_time
                    # Do not advance: retry the same offset on the shorter buffer.
                else:
                    pos += remove_len
            if self.out_of_budget():
                break
            remove_len //= 2

        removed = original_len - len(data)
        if removed > 0:
            tc.data = bytes(data)
            self.trimmed_bytes += removed
        return removed

    def fav_factor(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
        """AFL's favourite factor: execution time multiplied by size."""
        return max(tc.exec_time, 1e-6) * max(len(tc.data), 1)

    def update_bitmap_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
        """Keep, per edge, the smallest + fastest entry covering it."""
        factor = self.fav_factor(tc)
        for edge in tc.coverage:
            current = self.top_rated.get(edge)
            if current is not None and self.fav_factor(current) <= factor:
                continue
            self.top_rated[edge] = tc

    def cull_queue(self) -> List[TestCase]:
        """Greedy set cover over the queue: mark a minimal favoured subset.

        Walks the edges in id order, always picking the cheapest entry that
        covers a still-uncovered edge (AFL's cull_queue()).
        """
        for tc in self.queue:
            tc.is_favored = False
            tc.unique_edges = set()

        temp_v: Set[int] = set(self.bitmap.global_coverage)
        favored: List[TestCase] = []
        for edge in sorted(self.bitmap.global_coverage):
            if edge not in temp_v:
                continue
            best = self.top_rated.get(edge)
            if best is None:
                candidates = [tc for tc in self.queue if edge in tc.coverage]
                if not candidates:
                    continue
                best = min(candidates, key=lambda t: (self.fav_factor(t), t.creation_time))
            newly = temp_v & best.coverage
            temp_v -= best.coverage
            if not best.is_favored:
                best.is_favored = True
                best.unique_edges = set(newly)
                favored.append(best)
            else:
                best.unique_edges |= newly

        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for tc in self.queue if tc.is_favored and not tc.was_fuzzed)
        self.pending_not_fuzzed = sum(1 for tc in self.queue if not tc.was_fuzzed)
        return favored

    @property
    def favored_count(self) -> int:
        return sum(1 for tc in self.queue if tc.is_favored)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scheduling
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def select_next_seed(self) -> Optional[TestCase]:
        """Walk the queue honouring AFL's favoured-first skip probabilities."""
        if not self.queue:
            return None
        attempts = 0
        limit = max(4 * len(self.queue), 8)
        while attempts <= limit:
            attempts += 1
            if self.current_index >= len(self.queue):
                self.current_index = 0
                self.queue_cycle += 1
                self.cull_queue()
                if self.max_cycles is not None and self.queue_cycle > self.max_cycles:
                    return None
            tc = self.queue[self.current_index]
            self.current_index += 1
            if self.should_skip(tc):
                continue
            return tc
        return self.queue[0]

    def should_skip(self, tc: TestCase) -> bool:
        """AFL's skip logic: favoured entries first, 75/25 for the rest."""
        if self.pending_favored > 0:
            if (tc.was_fuzzed or not tc.is_favored) and self.rng.randint(0, 100) < SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB:
                return True
        elif not tc.is_favored and len(self.queue) > 10:
            if self.queue_cycle > 1 and not tc.was_fuzzed:
                if self.rng.randint(0, 100) < SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB:
                    return True
            else:
                if self.rng.randint(0, 100) < SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB:
                    return True
        return False

    def calculate_score(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
        """AFL's calculate_score(): exec speed, bitmap size, handicap, depth."""
        perf_score = 100.0
        avg_exec_time = (
            sum(q.exec_time for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue) if self.queue else tc.exec_time
        )
        avg_bitmap_size = (
            sum(len(q.coverage) for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue) if self.queue else 1.0
        )
        avg_exec_time = max(avg_exec_time, 1e-9)
        avg_bitmap_size = max(avg_bitmap_size, 1e-9)

        t = tc.exec_time
        if t * 0.1 > avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 10.0
        elif t * 0.25 > avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 25.0
        elif t * 0.5 > avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 50.0
        elif t * 0.75 > avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 75.0
        elif t * 4 < avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 300.0
        elif t * 3 < avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 200.0
        elif t * 2 < avg_exec_time:
            perf_score = 150.0

        bsize = len(tc.coverage)
        if bsize * 0.3 > avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 3.0
        elif bsize * 0.5 > avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 2.0
        elif bsize * 0.75 > avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 1.5
        elif bsize * 3 < avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 0.25
        elif bsize * 2 < avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 0.5
        elif bsize * 1.5 < avg_bitmap_size:
            perf_score *= 0.75

        handicap = getattr(tc, "handicap", 0)
        if handicap >= 4:
            perf_score *= 4.0
            tc.handicap = handicap - 4  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
        elif handicap:
            perf_score *= 2.0
            tc.handicap = handicap - 1  # type: ignore[attr-defined]

        depth = tc.depth
        if depth <= 3:
            pass
        elif depth <= 7:
            perf_score *= 2.0
        elif depth <= 13:
            perf_score *= 3.0
        elif depth <= 25:
            perf_score *= 4.0
        else:
            perf_score *= 5.0

        stability = getattr(tc, "stability", 100.0)
        if stability < 100.0:
            perf_score *= max(0.25, stability / 100.0)

        return min(perf_score, HAVOC_MAX_MULT * 100.0)

    def assign_energy(self, tc: TestCase) -> float:
        """Energy (havoc iterations budget) from the active power schedule."""
        energy = self.power_schedule.assign_energy(self, tc)
        self.energy_log.append(energy)
        return energy

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Deterministic stages
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def _set_stage(self, name: str) -> None:
        self.current_stage = name

    def stage_bitflip1(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
        """Walking 1 bit flips, with auto-dictionary token extraction."""
        self._set_stage("bitflip 1/1")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        nbits = len(data) * 8
        base_hash = coverage_hash(tc.coverage)
        prev_hash = base_hash
        collected = bytearray()

        for bit in range(nbits):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                return
            byte_idx, bit_idx = bit // 8, bit % 8
            data[byte_idx] ^= 1 << (7 - bit_idx)
            candidate = bytes(data)
            edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.run_target(candidate)
            self.save_if_interesting(candidate, edges, is_crash, exec_time, tc)
            data[byte_idx] ^= 1 << (7 - bit_idx)

            # Auto dictionary extraction (AFL's a_collect trick): a run of
            # consecutive bytes whose flips all perturb coverage identically
            # looks like a syntax token.
            cur_hash = coverage_hash(edges)
            if bit_idx == 7:
                if bit == nbits - 1 and cur_hash == prev_hash:
                    collected.append(data[byte_idx])
                    self._flush_auto(collected)
                elif cur_hash != prev_hash:
                    self._flush_auto(collected)
                    prev_hash = cur_hash
                if cur_hash != base_hash:
                    if len(collected) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
                        collected.append(data[byte_idx])
                    else:
                        self._flush_auto(collected)
                else:
                    self._flush_auto(collected)
        self._flush_auto(collected)

    def _flush_auto(self, collected: bytearray) -> None:
        if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= len(collected) <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
            self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(collected))
        collected.clear()

    def stage_bitflip2(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
        """Walking 2 bit flips."""
        self._set_stage("bitflip 2/1")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        nbits = len(data) * 8
        for bit in range(max(0, nbits - 1)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                return
            for off in (0, 1):
                idx = (bit + off) // 8
                data[idx] ^= 1 << (7 - (bit + off) % 8)
            candidate = bytes(data)
            self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc)
            for off in (0, 1):
                idx = (bit + off) // 8
                data[idx] ^= 1 << (7 - (bit + off) % 8)

    def stage_bitflip4(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
        """Walking 4 bit flips."""
        self._set_stage("bitflip 4/1")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        nbits = len(data) * 8
        for bit in range(max(0, nbits - 3)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                return
            for off in range(4):
                idx = (bit + off) // 8
                data[idx] ^= 1 << (7 - (bit + off) % 8)
            candidate = bytes(data)
            self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc)
            for off in range(4):
                idx = (bit + off) // 8
                data[idx] ^= 1 << (7 - (bit + off) % 8)

    def stage_byteflip8(self, tc: TestCase) -> List[int]:
        """Walking byte flips; builds the effector map used by later stages."""
        self._set_stage("bitflip 8/8")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        eff_map = [0] * max(1, len(data))
        if len(data):
            eff_map[0] = 1
            eff_map[-1] = 1
        base_hash = coverage_hash(tc.coverage)
        for i in range(len(data)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                break
            data[i] ^= 0xFF
            candidate = bytes(data)
            edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.run_target(candidate)
            self.save_if_interesting(candidate, edges, is_crash, exec_time, tc)
            if coverage_hash(edges) != base_hash:
                eff_map[i] = 1
            data[i] ^= 0xFF
        return eff_map

    def stage_byteflip16(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._set_stage("bitflip 16/8")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        for i in range(max(0, len(data) - 1)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                return
            if not eff_map[i] and not eff_map[i + 1]:
                continue
            data[i] ^= 0xFF
            data[i + 1] ^= 0xFF
            self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
            data[i] ^= 0xFF
            data[i + 1] ^= 0xFF

    def stage_byteflip32(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._set_stage("bitflip 32/8")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        for i in range(max(0, len(data) - 3)):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                return
            if not any(eff_map[i:i + 4]):
                continue
            for off in range(4):
                data[i + off] ^= 0xFF
            self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
            for off in range(4):
                data[i + off] ^= 0xFF

    def stage_arith8(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        """8 bit arithmetics: +/- 1..ARITH_MAX on every effective byte."""
        self._set_stage("arith 8/8")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        for i in range(len(data)):
            if not eff_map[i]:
                continue
            orig = data[i]
            for j in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                for value in ((orig + j) & 0xFF, (orig - j) & 0xFF):
                    if could_be_bitflip(orig ^ value):
                        continue
                    data[i] = value
                    self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
                    data[i] = orig

    def _read_int(self, data: bytearray, pos: int, width: int, little: bool) -> int:
        chunk = bytes(data[pos:pos + width])
        return int.from_bytes(chunk, "little" if little else "big")

    def _write_int(self, data: bytearray, pos: int, width: int, value: int, little: bool) -> None:
        data[pos:pos + width] = int(value % (1 << (8 * width))).to_bytes(
            width, "little" if little else "big"
        )

    def _stage_arith_wide(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int], width: int, label: str) -> None:
        self._set_stage(label)
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
        for i in range(max(0, len(data) - width + 1)):
            if not any(eff_map[i:i + width]):
                continue
            orig_bytes = bytes(data[i:i + width])
            orig_le = int.from_bytes(orig_bytes, "little")
            orig_be = int.from_bytes(orig_bytes, "big")
            for j in range(1, ARITH_MAX + 1):
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                for little in (True, False):
                    base = orig_le if little else orig_be
                    for value in ((base + j) & mask, (base - j) & mask):
                        as_le = value if little else int(
                            value.to_bytes(width, "big")[::-1].hex() or "0", 16
                        )
                        if little:
                            new_le = value
                        else:
                            new_le = int.from_bytes(value.to_bytes(width, "big"), "little")
                        if could_be_bitflip(orig_le ^ new_le):
                            continue
                        if not little and could_be_arith(orig_le, new_le, width):
                            # Already covered by the little-endian pass.
                            continue
                        del as_le
                        self._write_int(data, i, width, value, little)
                        self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
                        data[i:i + width] = orig_bytes

    def stage_arith16(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._stage_arith_wide(tc, eff_map, 2, "arith 16/8")

    def stage_arith32(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._stage_arith_wide(tc, eff_map, 4, "arith 32/8")

    def stage_interest8(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        """Overwrite single bytes with AFL's interesting 8 bit values."""
        self._set_stage("interest 8/8")
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        for i in range(len(data)):
            if not eff_map[i]:
                continue
            orig = data[i]
            for interesting in INTERESTING_8:
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                value = interesting & 0xFF
                if could_be_bitflip(orig ^ value) or could_be_arith(orig, value, 1):
                    continue
                data[i] = value
                self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
                data[i] = orig

    def _stage_interest_wide(
        self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int], width: int, values: Sequence[int], label: str
    ) -> None:
        self._set_stage(label)
        data = bytearray(tc.data)
        mask = (1 << (8 * width)) - 1
        for i in range(max(0, len(data) - width + 1)):
            if not any(eff_map[i:i + width]):
                continue
            orig_bytes = bytes(data[i:i + width])
            orig_le = int.from_bytes(orig_bytes, "little")
            for interesting in values:
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                for little in (True, False):
                    value = interesting & mask
                    new_bytes = int(value).to_bytes(width, "little" if little else "big")
                    new_le = int.from_bytes(new_bytes, "little")
                    if new_le == orig_le:
                        continue
                    if could_be_bitflip(orig_le ^ new_le):
                        continue
                    if could_be_arith(orig_le, new_le, width):
                        continue
                    if not little and could_be_interest(orig_le, new_le, width, False):
                        continue
                    data[i:i + width] = new_bytes
                    self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(data), tc)
                    data[i:i + width] = orig_bytes

    def stage_interest16(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._stage_interest_wide(tc, eff_map, 2, INTERESTING_16, "interest 16/8")

    def stage_interest32(self, tc: TestCase, eff_map: List[int]) -> None:
        self._stage_interest_wide(tc, eff_map, 4, INTERESTING_32, "interest 32/8")

    def stage_dictionary(self, tc: TestCase, use_auto: bool = False) -> None:
        """Overwrite/insert user (``-x``) or auto-extracted dictionary tokens."""
        tokens = self.dictionary.auto_extras if use_auto else self.dictionary.extras
        if not tokens:
            return
        self._set_stage("auto extras (over)" if use_auto else "user extras (over)")
        limit = MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS if use_auto else MAX_DET_EXTRAS
        data = bytes(tc.data)
        for i in range(len(data)):
            for token in tokens[:limit]:
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                if i + len(token) > len(data):
                    continue
                candidate = data[:i] + token + data[i + len(token):]
                if candidate == data:
                    continue
                self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc)
        if use_auto:
            return
        # User extras are also inserted (growing the input).
        self._set_stage("user extras (insert)")
        for i in range(len(data) + 1):
            for token in tokens[:limit]:
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    return
                candidate = data[:i] + token + data[i:]
                self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc)

    def run_deterministic_stages(self, tc: TestCase) -> None:
        """The full deterministic pipeline in AFL's order."""
        self.stage_bitflip1(tc)
        self.stage_bitflip2(tc)
        self.stage_bitflip4(tc)
        eff_map = self.stage_byteflip8(tc)
        self.stage_byteflip16(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_byteflip32(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_arith8(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_arith16(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_arith32(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_interest8(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_interest16(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_interest32(tc, eff_map)
        self.stage_dictionary(tc, use_auto=False)
        self.stage_dictionary(tc, use_auto=True)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Havoc / splice
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def havoc_mutate(
        self,
        data: bytes,
        num_ops: Optional[int] = None,
        allowed_positions: Optional[Set[int]] = None,
    ) -> bytes:
        """Apply a stack of 2^1..2^7 random mutations (AFL's havoc).

        ``allowed_positions`` restricts byte-modifying operators to a subset of
        offsets; FairFuzz uses it to preserve influential bytes.
        """
        rng = self.rng
        if num_ops is None:
            num_ops = 1 << (1 + rng.randint(0, HAVOC_STACK_POW2))
        out = bytearray(data if data else b"\x00")

        def pick_pos(limit: int) -> int:
            if limit <= 0:
                return 0
            if allowed_positions:
                choices = sorted(p for p in allowed_positions if p < limit)
                if choices:
                    return int(choices[rng.randint(0, len(choices))])
            return int(rng.randint(0, limit))

        length_ops_allowed = allowed_positions is None
        num_operators = 15 if length_ops_allowed else 11

        for _ in range(num_ops):
            if not out:
                out = bytearray(b"\x00")
            op = rng.randint(0, num_operators)
            if op == 0:  # flip a single bit
                pos = pick_pos(len(out))
                out[pos] ^= 1 << rng.randint(0, 8)
            elif op == 1:  # set an interesting 8 bit value
                pos = pick_pos(len(out))
                out[pos] = INTERESTING_8[rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_8))] & 0xFF
            elif op == 2:  # set an interesting 16 bit value
                if len(out) >= 2:
                    pos = pick_pos(len(out) - 1)
                    value = INTERESTING_16[rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_16))] & 0xFFFF
                    order = "little" if rng.randint(0, 2) else "big"
                    out[pos:pos + 2] = value.to_bytes(2, order)
            elif op == 3:  # set an interesting 32 bit value
                if len(out) >= 4:
                    pos = pick_pos(len(out) - 3)
                    value = INTERESTING_32[rng.randint(0, len(INTERESTING_32))] & 0xFFFFFFFF
                    order = "little" if rng.randint(0, 2) else "big"
                    out[pos:pos + 4] = value.to_bytes(4, order)
            elif op == 4:  # subtract from a byte
                pos = pick_pos(len(out))
                out[pos] = (out[pos] - (1 + rng.randint(0, ARITH_MAX))) & 0xFF
            elif op == 5:  # add to a byte
                pos = pick_pos(len(out))
                out[pos] = (out[pos] + (1 + rng.randint(0, ARITH_MAX))) & 0xFF
            elif op == 6:  # 16 bit arithmetics
                if len(out) >= 2:
                    pos = pick_pos(len(out) - 1)
                    order = "little" if rng.randint(0, 2) else "big"
                    value = int.from_bytes(bytes(out[pos:pos + 2]), order)
                    delta = 1 + rng.randint(0, ARITH_MAX)
                    if rng.randint(0, 2):
                        value = (value + delta) & 0xFFFF
                    else:
                        value = (value - delta) & 0xFFFF
                    out[pos:pos + 2] = value.to_bytes(2, order)
            elif op == 7:  # 32 bit arithmetics
                if len(out) >= 4:
                    pos = pick_pos(len(out) - 3)
                    order = "little" if rng.randint(0, 2) else "big"
                    value = int.from_bytes(bytes(out[pos:pos + 4]), order)
                    delta = 1 + rng.randint(0, ARITH_MAX)
                    if rng.randint(0, 2):
                        value = (value + delta) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                    else:
                        value = (value - delta) & 0xFFFFFFFF
                    out[pos:pos + 4] = value.to_bytes(4, order)
            elif op == 8:  # random byte (XOR with 1..255)
                pos = pick_pos(len(out))
                out[pos] ^= 1 + rng.randint(0, 255)
            elif op == 9:  # overwrite with a repeated byte / copied chunk
                if len(out) > 1:
                    size = min(len(out), 1 + rng.randint(0, HAVOC_BLK_SMALL))
                    dst = pick_pos(max(1, len(out) - size + 1))
                    if rng.randint(0, 4):
                        src = pick_pos(max(1, len(out) - size + 1))
                        out = bytearray(clone_bytes(bytes(out), src, dst, size))
                    else:
                        value = rng.randint(0, 256)
                        for k in range(size):
                            if dst + k < len(out):
                                out[dst + k] = value
            elif op == 10:  # dictionary token overwrite
                tokens = self.dictionary.all_tokens
                if tokens:
                    token = tokens[rng.randint(0, len(tokens))]
                    if len(token) <= len(out):
                        pos = pick_pos(len(out) - len(token) + 1)
                        out[pos:pos + len(token)] = token
            elif op == 11:  # delete bytes
                if len(out) > TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
                    size = 1 + rng.randint(0, min(HAVOC_BLK_SMALL, len(out) - 1))
                    pos = int(rng.randint(0, max(1, len(out) - size + 1)))
                    out = bytearray(delete_bytes(bytes(out), pos, size))
            elif op == 12:  # clone / insert a block
                size = 1 + rng.randint(0, min(HAVOC_BLK_SMALL, max(1, len(out))))
                pos = int(rng.randint(0, len(out) + 1))
                if rng.randint(0, 4):
                    src = int(rng.randint(0, max(1, len(out))))
                    chunk = bytes(out[src:src + size]) or b"\x00"
                else:
                    chunk = bytes([rng.randint(0, 256)]) * size
                out = bytearray(insert_bytes(bytes(out), pos, chunk))
            elif op == 13:  # dictionary token insert
                tokens = self.dictionary.all_tokens
                if tokens:
                    token = tokens[rng.randint(0, len(tokens))]
                    pos = int(rng.randint(0, len(out) + 1))
                    out = bytearray(insert_bytes(bytes(out), pos, token))
            else:  # op == 14: swap two bytes
                if len(out) >= 2:
                    a = pick_pos(len(out))
                    b = pick_pos(len(out))
                    out[a], out[b] = out[b], out[a]

        return bytes(out)

    def stage_havoc(self, tc: TestCase, energy: float) -> int:
        """Random stacked mutations; the number of execs scales with energy."""
        self._set_stage("havoc")
        iterations = int(max(HAVOC_MIN, HAVOC_CYCLES * energy / 100.0))
        iterations = min(iterations, self.budget_left())
        finds = 0
        for _ in range(iterations):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                break
            candidate = self.havoc_mutate(tc.data)
            if self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc):
                finds += 1
        return finds

    def stage_splice(self, tc: TestCase, energy: float = 100.0) -> int:
        """Splice the entry with another queue entry, then havoc the result."""
        if len(self.queue) < 2:
            return 0
        self._set_stage("splice")
        finds = 0
        for _ in range(SPLICE_CYCLES):
            if self.out_of_budget():
                break
            other = self.queue[self.rng.randint(0, len(self.queue))]
            if other is tc or len(other.data) < 2 or len(tc.data) < 2:
                continue
            spliced = self.splice_inputs(tc.data, other.data)
            if spliced is None:
                continue
            rounds = int(max(1, min(SPLICE_HAVOC * energy / 100.0, self.budget_left())))
            for _ in range(min(rounds, SPLICE_HAVOC)):
                if self.out_of_budget():
                    break
                candidate = self.havoc_mutate(spliced)
                if self.common_fuzz_stuff(candidate, tc):
                    finds += 1
        return finds

    def splice_inputs(self, a: bytes, b: bytes) -> Optional[bytes]:
        """Combine two inputs at a random midpoint (AFL's splice stage)."""
        if len(a) < 2 or len(b) < 2:
            return None
        # AFL looks for the first and last differing byte and splices in between.
        limit = min(len(a), len(b))
        first_diff = last_diff = -1
        for i in range(limit):
            if a[i] != b[i]:
                if first_diff < 0:
                    first_diff = i
                last_diff = i
        if first_diff < 0 or last_diff < first_diff + 1:
            split = int(self.rng.randint(1, limit))
        else:
            split = int(first_diff + self.rng.randint(0, last_diff - first_diff))
            split = max(1, min(split, limit - 1)) if limit > 1 else 1
        return a[:split] + b[split:]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Main loop
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def fuzz_one(self, tc: Optional[TestCase] = None) -> int:
        """Fuzz a single queue entry through every enabled stage."""
        if tc is None:
            tc = self.select_next_seed()
        if tc is None:
            return 0
        self.current_target = tc
        tc.times_chosen += 1
        tc.fuzz_count += 1
        before = len(self.queue)

        energy = self.assign_energy(tc)
        if energy <= 0:
            tc.was_fuzzed = True
            return 0

        if self.deterministic and not tc.was_fuzzed:
            self.run_deterministic_stages(tc)
        self.stage_havoc(tc, energy)
        if self.use_splice:
            self.stage_splice(tc, energy)

        tc.was_fuzzed = True
        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for q in self.queue if q.is_favored and not q.was_fuzzed)
        return len(self.queue) - before

    def run(self, max_execs: Optional[int] = None) -> FuzzerStats:
        """Run the campaign until the exec budget (or cycle cap) is exhausted."""
        if max_execs is not None:
            self.max_execs = max_execs
        self.cull_queue()
        while not self.out_of_budget():
            tc = self.select_next_seed()
            if tc is None:
                break
            self.fuzz_one(tc)
            if self.stop_on_crash and self.first_crash_exec is not None:
                break
            if self.max_cycles is not None and self.queue_cycle > self.max_cycles:
                break
        return self.get_stats()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Reporting
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    def get_stats(self) -> FuzzerStats:
        stability = (
            sum(self.stability_samples) / len(self.stability_samples)
            if self.stability_samples
            else 100.0
        )
        elapsed = max(self.fork_server.total_time, 1e-9)
        return FuzzerStats(
            total_execs=self.total_execs,
            paths_discovered=len(self.queue),
            corpus_size=len(self.queue),
            unique_crashes=len(self.unique_crash_hashes),
            total_crashes=self.total_crashes,
            edges_covered=self.bitmap.get_coverage_count(),
            edge_coverage=self.bitmap.get_coverage_percentage(self.total_edges),
            queue_cycles=self.queue_cycle,
            first_crash_exec=self.first_crash_exec,
            favored_count=self.favored_count,
            stability=stability,
            trimmed_bytes=self.trimmed_bytes,
            havoc_finds=self.stage_finds.get("havoc", 0),
            splice_finds=self.stage_finds.get("splice", 0),
            det_finds=sum(
                count
                for name, count in self.stage_finds.items()
                if name not in ("havoc", "splice", "init")
            ),
            stage_finds=dict(self.stage_finds),
            stage_execs=dict(self.stage_execs),
            auto_extras=len(self.dictionary.auto_extras),
            mean_energy=(sum(self.energy_log) / len(self.energy_log)) if self.energy_log else 0.0,
            execs_per_sec=self.total_execs / elapsed,
        )

    def get_coverage(self) -> Set[int]:
        return set(self.bitmap.global_coverage)

    def corpus_data(self) -> List[bytes]:
        return [tc.data for tc in self.queue]

"""Core AFL (American Fuzzy Lop) coverage-guided greybox fuzzer.

This module is a faithful, deterministic simulation of afl-fuzz.c's algorithm:

* 64KB shared-memory edge bitmap with hit-count bucketing
  (1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+),
* edge identification via ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` (AFL's
  ``prev_loc``/``cur_loc`` trick, usually written ``(prev ^ cur) >> 1``),
* a fork-server model that amortises target start-up cost,
* test-case calibration with multi-run stability detection,
* input trimming with powers-of-two block removal preserving coverage,
* corpus culling via greedy set cover (smallest + fastest entry per edge),
* the complete deterministic stage pipeline (walking bit flips 1/2/4, byte
  flips 8/16/32, arithmetics +/- 1..35 for 8/16/32 bit widths in both
  endiannesses, interesting values 8/16/32, auto-dictionary extraction during
  the bit-flip stage and user/auto dictionary insertion),
* the havoc stage (2^1..2^7 stacked random mutations),
* the splice stage (midpoint recombination of two queue entries + havoc),
* performance scoring from execution speed / bitmap size / depth / handicap,
* crash de-duplication through coverage hashing,
* and queue scheduling with favoured-seed priority (the 75/25 skip split).

Everything is driven from a single ``numpy.random.RandomState`` so that a given
seed always produces the same run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Callable, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple

import numpy as np

from fuzzsim.bitmap import MAP_SIZE
from fuzzsim.mutation import (
    INTERESTING_8,
    INTERESTING_16,
    INTERESTING_32,
    clone_bytes,
    delete_bytes,
    insert_bytes,
)
from fuzzsim.seed import TestCase

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# AFL tuning constants (config.h)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

ARITH_MAX = 35            # maximum offset used by the arithmetic stages
HAVOC_STACK_POW2 = 7      # havoc stacks 2^1 .. 2^7 mutations
HAVOC_CYCLES = 256        # base havoc iterations (scaled by performance score)
HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT = 1024  # havoc iterations when deterministic stages are off
HAVOC_MIN = 16            # never do fewer than this many havoc execs
HAVOC_MAX_MULT = 16       # performance score cap multiplier (=> max 1600)
HAVOC_BLK_SMALL = 32
HAVOC_BLK_MEDIUM = 128
HAVOC_BLK_LARGE = 1500
SPLICE_CYCLES = 15        # splice attempts per queue entry
SPLICE_HAVOC = 32         # havoc iterations applied to a spliced input

SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB = 75     # favoured/unseen entries: 75/25 split
SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB = 95   # skip probability for old non-favoured entries
SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB = 75   # skip probability for fresh non-favoured entries

CAL_CYCLES = 3            # calibration executions for a fresh entry
TRIM_MIN_BYTES = 4
TRIM_START_STEPS = 16
TRIM_END_STEPS = 1024

MIN_AUTO_EXTRA = 3
MAX_AUTO_EXTRA = 32
MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS = 50      # auto dictionary capacity
MAX_DET_EXTRAS = 200      # deterministic extras cut-off

# Hit-count buckets used by AFL's classify_counts().
COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS: Tuple[Tuple[int, int, int], ...] = (
    (0, 0, 0),        # never executed
    (1, 1, 1),        # exactly once
    (2, 2, 2),        # twice
    (3, 3, 4),        # three times
    (4, 7, 8),        # 4-7
    (8, 15, 16),      # 8-15
    (16, 31, 32),     # 16-31
    (32, 127, 64),    # 32-127
    (128, 1 << 30, 128),  # 128+
)


def classify_counts(count: int) -> int:
    """Map a raw hit count onto AFL's 8 hit-count buckets.

    AFL folds hit counts into powers-of-two-ish buckets so that small changes
    in loop trip counts do not look like new coverage::

        1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+
    """
    if count < 0:
        raise ValueError("hit count must be non-negative")
    for low, high, bucket in COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS:
        if low <= count <= high:
            return bucket
    return 128


def bucket_index(count: int) -> int:
    """Return the index (0..8) of the bucket a hit count falls into."""
    for idx, (low, high, _bucket) in enumerate(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS):
        if low <= count <= high:
            return idx
    return len(COUNT_CLASS_BUCKETS) - 1


def edge_hash(prev_block: int, cur_block: int, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE) -> int:
    """Compute AFL's edge id for the transition ``prev_block -> cur_block``.

    AFL's instrumentation keeps ``prev_loc`` already shifted right by one so
    that A->B and B->A hash differently; the transition is therefore
    ``(prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block`` taken modulo the bitmap size.
    """
    return ((prev_block >> 1) ^ cur_block) % map_size


def coverage_hash(edges: Iterable[int]) -> str:
    """Stable hash of a coverage set, used for crash de-duplication."""
    payload = ",".join(str(e) for e in sorted(edges)).encode()
    return hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:16]


def swap16(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 16 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFF
    return ((value & 0xFF) << 8) | (value >> 8)


def swap32(value: int) -> int:
    """Byte-swap a 32 bit value."""
    value &= 0xFFFFFFFF
    return (
        ((value & 0x000000FF) << 24)
        | ((value & 0x0000FF00) << 8)
        | ((value & 0x00FF0000) >> 8)
        | ((value & 0xFF000000) >> 24)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# "Could this value have been produced by a cheaper stage?" predicates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``xor_val`` is reachable by the walking bit-flip stages."""
    if xor_val == 0:
        return True
    # Shift right until we hit the first set bit.
    sh = 0
    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
        sh += 1
        xor_val >>= 1
    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15, 255):
        return True
    # 16 and 32 bit flips are only tried on aligned offsets.
    if xor_val == 0xFFFF and sh % 16 == 0:
        return True
    if xor_val == 0xFFFFFFFF and sh % 32 == 0:
        return True
    return False


def could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the arithmetic stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    diffs = 0
    ov = nv = 0
    for i in range(blen):
        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b

    # A single byte differs: an 8 bit arithmetic op would have found it.
    if diffs == 1:
        if abs(ov - nv) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True

    if blen == 1:
        return False

    # Try 16 bit arithmetics in both endiannesses.
    diffs = 0
    for i in range(blen // 2):
        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
        if a != b:
            diffs += 1
            ov, nv = a, b
    if diffs == 1:
        if abs(ov - nv) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
        if abs(swap16(ov) - swap16(nv)) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True

    if blen == 4:
        if abs(old_val - new_val) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
        if abs(swap32(old_val) - swap32(new_val)) <= ARITH_MAX:
            return True
    return False


def could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
    """True if ``old_val -> new_val`` is reachable by the interesting-value stages."""
    if old_val == new_val:
        return True

    # Single-byte interesting values applied at any offset.
    for i in range(blen):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_8:
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((interesting & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True

    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
        return False

    for i in range(blen - 1):
        for interesting in INTERESTING_16:
            iv = interesting & 0xFFFF
            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (iv << (8 * i))
            if new_val == tval:
                return True
            if blen > 2:
                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swap16(iv) << (8 * i))
                if new_val == tval:
                    return True
    return False


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fork server simulation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class ForkServer:
    """Simulated AFL fork server.

    The real fork server executes the target up to ``main()`` once and then
    clones the initialised process for every test case, which removes the
    (expensive) linking/initialisation cost from the per-exec budget.  We model
    that: ``STARTUP_COST`` is paid once at ``start()`` and every subsequent run
    only pays ``FORK_COST`` plus the target's own execution time.
    """

    STARTUP_COST = 0.020  # 20ms one-off initialisation
    FORK_COST = 0.0002    # 0.2ms per fork
    EXECVE_COST = 0.010   # 10ms if we had to execve() every time

    def __init__(self, program):
        self.program = program
        self.is_running = False
        self.total_execs = 0
        self.total_time = 0.0
        self.startup_time = 0.0
        self.timeouts = 0
        self.child_pid = 0

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Spin up the fork server (paid once)."""
        if self.is_running:
            return
        self.is_running = True
        self.startup_time = self.STARTUP_COST
        self.total_time += self.STARTUP_COST
        self.child_pid = 1000

    def run(self, data: bytes) -> Tuple[Set[int], bool, float]:
        """Execute one test case through the fork server."""
        if not self.is_running:
            self.start()
        self.child_pid += 1
        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.program.execute(data)
        self.total_execs += 1
        self.total_time += self.FORK_COST + exec_time
        return set(edges), bool(is_crash), float(exec_time)

    def stop(self) -> None:
        self.is_running = False
        self.child_pid = 0

    @property
    def saved_time(self) -> float:
        """Time saved compared to a plain execve() based executor."""
        return self.total_execs * (self.EXECVE_COST - self.FORK_COST) - self.STARTUP_COST


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Bitmap with hit-count bucketing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class AFLBitmap:
    """64KB coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing and virgin-bit tracking."""

    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
        self.map_size = map_size
        # virgin_bits[edge] is the OR of every bucket value observed so far.
        self.virgin_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.global_coverage: Set[int] = set()
        self.hit_counts: Dict[int, int] = {}
        self.trace_bits: Dict[int, int] = {}

    # -- current run ------------------------------------------------------
    def reset_trace(self) -> None:
        self.trace_bits = {}

    def record_trace(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> None:
        """Store the raw hit counts of the current execution."""
        self.trace_bits = dict(edges)

    def classified_trace(self) -> Dict[int, int]:
        """Return the current trace after classify_counts()."""
        return {e: classify_counts(c) for e, c in self.trace_bits.items()}

    # -- global bitmap ----------------------------------------------------
    def has_new_bits(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
        """AFL's has_new_bits(): 2 = new edge, 1 = new hit-count bucket, 0 = nothing."""
        result = 0
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            bucket = classify_counts(count)
            seen = self.virgin_bits.get(edge, 0)
            if seen == 0:
                return 2
            if seen & bucket == 0:
                result = max(result, 1)
        return result

    def update(self, edges: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
        """Fold an execution into the global bitmap, returning new edges."""
        new_edges = set()
        for edge, count in edges.items():
            if count <= 0:
                continue
            if edge not in self.virgin_bits:
                new_edges.add(edge)
                self.virgin_bits[edge] = 0
            self.virgin_bits[edge] |= classify_counts(count)
            self.global_coverage.add(edge)
            self.hit_counts[edge] = self.hit_counts.get(edge, 0) + count
        return new_edges

    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
        """Number of non-zero bytes in the bitmap (AFL's count_bytes)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_count(self) -> int:
        return len(self.global_coverage)

    def get_coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
        if total_edges == 0:
            return 0.0
        return len(self.global_coverage) / total_edges * 100.0

    def map_density(self) -> float:
        """Fraction of the 64KB map that is in use (AFL's map density stat)."""
        return len(self.global_coverage) / self.map_size * 100.0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Dictionary (user supplied extras + auto-extracted tokens)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class Dictionary:
    """User (``-x``) and auto-extracted dictionary tokens."""

    def __init__(self, extras: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None):
        self.extras: List[bytes] = sorted(set(extras or []), key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        self.auto_extras: List[bytes] = []
        self.auto_hits: Dict[bytes, int] = {}

    def maybe_add_auto(self, token: bytes) -> bool:
        """AFL's maybe_add_auto(): remember a token found during bit flipping."""
        if not (MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= len(token) <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA):
            return False
        if len(set(token)) <= 1:  # all-same bytes carry no information
            return False
        if token in self.extras:
            return False
        if token in self.auto_hits:
            self.auto_hits[token] += 1
            return False
        self.auto_hits[token] = 1
        if len(self.auto_extras) < MAX_AUTO_EXTRAS:
            self.auto_extras.append(token)
            self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
            return True
        # Replace the least useful (largest) entry.
        self.auto_extras[-1] = token
        self.auto_extras.sort(key=lambda t: (len(t), t))
        return True

    @property
    def all_tokens(self) -> List[bytes]:
        return list(self.extras) + list(self.auto_extras)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self.extras) + len(self.auto_extras)
